subject: Request: uptime remedy variance and latency concession for Orion Biotech
messages:
From: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@orionbio.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orionbio.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Uptime & latency remedies for contract - need variance

Hi Lauren / Aditya,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. We're very close on commercial terms but procurement raised a hard stop on the proposed uptime remedy table in the standard SOW — specifically the step-down credits tied to brief outages and the latency remedy language. Our legal team is asking whether Redwood can agree to a narrower remedy profile and a firm cap on cumulative credits so this doesn't put an unbounded exposure on us.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood reduce the uptime threshold to 99.95% for the Dedicated cluster assigned to Orion (instead of 99.99%)?
- Can remedies be capped at a maximum of 6 months of invoice credits across any 12-month period, and can latency remedies be limited to a service-credit approach rather than unlimited termination or RTO-style remediations?

I've attached our redline of the SLA and the procurement team's one-pager. We need to present an executed amendment to legal by COB Monday to keep our quarter close. Please let me know if this is something your deal desk / execs can approve conditionally.

Attachments:
- SLA_Remedies_Orion_v2.pdf (pdf)

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Claire Jensen
VP, Strategic Partnerships
Orion Biotech
claire.jensen@orionbio.com
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@orionbio.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Uptime & latency remedies for contract - need variance

Claire — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the redline. We're eager to close this with Orion. I'll loop in Deal Desk (Aditya) and Ops risk (Marcus) to confirm the mitigation and cost impact. A few quick clarifying questions before we escalate for exec approval:

1) Is the 99.95% ask intended as the long-term target in the SOW or only for the first 12 months while you ramp?
2) When you say "latency remedies limited to service-credit approach," do you mean a fixed percentage credit for sustained P95/P99 breaches rather than variable SLA termination remedies?

Internally I'll propose a conditional deviation (99.95% uptime for the dedicated pool, remedies capped at 6 months' credits across 12 months, latency credit-based remediation only). I'll attach the internal deal summary. If Aditya/Marcus are comfortable, I'll take this to the execs for signoff today.

Next steps: I will prepare a redline for the amendment and mark it as contingent on one-time concession terms.

Attachments:
- deal_summary_ORION_Q4.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Uptime & latency remedies for contract - need variance (internal)

Lauren / Marcus — reviewed Claire's note and the attached redline. Summary of operational/risk perspective:

- 99.95% for a dedicated environment is a reasonable, negotiable compromise if we can limit the exposure. Historically, our Dedicated customers running production workloads expect 99.99%, but for specialized regulated customers with strict procurement needs we have precedent for 99.95%.
- Remedies: cap at "aggregate service credits not to exceed six months' worth of monthly recurring revenue (MRR) within any rolling 12-month period" is acceptable from a deal-desk standpoint. Recommend clarifying that credits are calculated as a percentage of monthly invoice and that they are the exclusive remedy (no termination right tied to uptime breaches).
- Latency: convert latency thresholds into a tiered credit schedule (e.g., P99 sustained > 2x baseline for >30 minutes => small % monthly credit) and explicitly exclude unlimited termination or SLA-driven refunds beyond the six-month cap.

Commercial recommendation to present to execs:
- Approve deviation to 99.95% uptime for 12 months (with review at renewal).
- Remedies capped at 6 months' MRR across any 12-month rolling window.
- Latency remediation limited to service credits only; provide sample credit table.
- In exchange: offer a one-time onboarding discount of 10% for the first 3 billing cycles and a 30-day advanced support onboarding package.

Cost/risk note: this introduces limited additional exposure but should be contained via the cap and exclusive-credit remedy. If accepted, ask legal to produce a short amendment and Finance to sign off on the onboarding concession.

Aditya Rao
Senior Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@orionbio.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@orionbio.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Approved: conditional uptime & latency remedy amendment (next steps)

Claire / Tom — thanks for your patience. After internal review with Deal Desk and Ops, we can approve a conditional variance to the standard SOW as follows: 

- Uptime target: 99.95% for the Dedicated cluster assigned to Orion for the initial 12-month term (to be reviewed at renewal).
- Remedies: aggregate service credits limited to a maximum equal to six months' MRR across any rolling 12-month period; credits calculated as a percentage of monthly invoice and are the exclusive monetary remedy for uptime breaches (no termination right tied to uptime breaches).
- Latency: convert latency remediation to a tiered service-credit schedule (credit percentages tied to severity and duration). Latency credits are included in the six-month aggregate cap.
- Commercial concession: one-time 10% onboarding credit applied to the first 3 invoices and an onboarding success package (30 days of priority support).

Conditions / required items before amendment becomes effective:
1) Orion to sign the attached SLA amendment and the corresponding SOW addendum in DocuSign (link below).
2) Orion to provide the staging/perf ramp plan and a short PoC run for the dedicated pool so Ops can validate baseline latency within 30 days of activation.
3) Finance approval on the onboarding credit (already requested).

We will route the amendment through Legal for a short-form redline (no other changes to indemnities or data residency). Once DocuSign is returned, we'll set the Dedicated cluster provisioning schedule.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/xyz/Orion-SLA-Amendment
Attachments:
- approved_sla_amendment_Orion_20261120.pdf (pdf)

If this works, Claire please confirm and we will push the DocuSign package for signatures. Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting Orion live.
